item.title: One-China principle emphasized
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
One-China principle emphasized Cross-Strait representatives gathered on Sunday to mark the 81st anniversary of Taiwan's restoration to the motherland, stressing that both sides belong to one China and expressing firm opposition to "Taiwan independence" separatism and external interference. A symposium in Fu-zhou, Fujian province, brought together around 200 attendees, including descendants of revolutionary martyrs who sacrificed their lives in Taiwan and Taiwan compatriots who resisted Japanese aggression, cross-Strait youth, experts, scholars and representatives from the Hong Kong and Macao special administrative regions and overseas. The event came one year after a decision by the national legislature to designate Oct 25 as the Commemoration Day of Taiwan's Restoration, the day in 1945 when Taiwan was officially returned to China after half a century of Japanese colonial occupation. Song Tao, head of the Taiwan Work Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said that the establishment of the commemorative day demonstrated the country's firm confidence in defending its sovereignty and territorial integrity, and solidified the international community's adherence to the one-China principle. Song emphasized that compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Strait must jointly carry forward the great spirit of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression (1931-45), while firmly opposing "Taiwan independence" separatism and external interference. It is essential to promote Chinese culture to strengthen national pride and boost the confidence of the Chinese people, he said, adding that the Chinese mainland will firmly support the patriotic reunification forces within the island and steadfastly advance national reunification. Hung Hsiu-chu, former chairwoman of the Chinese Kuomintang party, recalled the crimes committed by the Japanese aggressors against Chinese people and warned that people must remain strictly vigilant against Japan's attempts to revive militarism. Hung criticized Taiwan's current Democratic Progressive Party authorities for attempting to erase the history of the war against Japanese invasion and Taiwan's restoration from the school curriculum, which she said left younger generations unaware of their roots and created a confused identity that remained a fundamental cause of Taiwan's internal rift and cross-Strait tensions. Ou Kuei-chih, a retired Chinese literature teacher from Taipei First Girls' High School, said that only by learning history can young people discover their roots, understand the past suffering of the nation, and find answers on how to avoid the danger of war caused by cross-Strait division. Encouraging Taiwan youths to visit the mainland for more exchanges, she said students must break through the bias of the island's media to search for the truth, explore why textbooks differ, and make their own rational judgments. Chiu Chih-shien, secretary-general of the Taiwan Restoration Commemoration Association, said that Taiwan's restoration was a core achievement of the war against Japanese aggression, noting that this historic day was once widely celebrated through various public activities before the DPP's deliberate erasure led to its gradual fading from public memory over the past decades. Chiu said that the legislation last year had prompted many Taiwan compatriots to reflect on why local textbooks and media in Taiwan remained silent while the mainland highly valued the anniversary, inspiring people to recognize its true historical value. He added that civic groups on the island should work together to hold more public activities so that people can learn the real history and understand how restoration benefits them.

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: Marking Taiwan Recovery Day with shared resolve to advance China's reunification
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25
Xinhua Commentary: Marking Taiwan Recovery Day with shared resolve to advance China's reunification Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-10-25
BEIJING, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- As China prepares to mark the 81st anniversary of its recovery of Taiwan and observe the Taiwan Recovery Day on Oct. 25, the occasion offers an opportunity to revisit a glorious chapter of history, in which people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait jointly resisted foreign aggression, and to draw strength from the past to advance reunification. China's recovery of Taiwan in 1945 was a hard-won victory in the Chinese people's resistance against Japanese aggression during World War II, and a defining moment in the nation's struggle to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity. Starting in 1840, China endured a period of immense suffering amid foreign aggression and the decay of feudal rule. Japan's aggression marked some of the darkest chapters in modern Chinese history. Following its war against China in 1894, Japan seized Taiwan and the Penghu Islands in 1895, subjecting Taiwan to five decades of colonial rule. Faced with both internal turmoil and foreign invasion, the Chinese people valiantly fought against the invaders, ultimately defeating Japanese aggression to safeguard the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity. On Oct. 25, 1945, after China's victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the broader World Anti-Fascist War, Taiwan was recovered. This historic day, forever etched in the history of the Chinese nation, deserves to be remembered by people on both sides of the Strait. Throughout the struggles against foreign aggression and for national liberation, Taiwan shared the fate of its motherland China. Patriots in Taiwan resisted Japanese colonial rule through political, military and cultural struggles, with more than 650,000 giving their lives during the five decades of Japanese occupation. Driven by the conviction that "to save Taiwan, one must first save the motherland," over 50,000 people in Taiwan went across the Strait to join the fight against Japanese aggression, risking their lives to defend the dignity and honor of the Chinese nation. Historical archives and photographs capture the island's jubilant celebrations when China recovered Taiwan in 1945. Families decorated their homes with lanterns, brought out ancestral tablets, and burned incense to share the good news with their forebears. Residents poured spontaneously into streets to cheer, while the sound of firecrackers rang out into the night. These memories, forged through bloodshed and sacrifice, testify to the deep-rooted bonds between people in Taiwan and their fellow Chinese on the mainland, as well as the shared destiny of people on both sides of the Strait. China's recovery of Taiwan was an important outcome of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, and provides compelling evidence that the Chinese government resumed the exercise of sovereignty over Taiwan. The Cairo Declaration, issued in 1943, stipulates that all territories Japan had stolen from China, including Taiwan and the Penghu Islands, shall be restored to China. The Potsdam Proclamation of 1945 reiterates that "the terms of the Cairo Declaration shall be carried out." In September 1945, Japan signed the instrument of surrender, pledging to fulfill the obligations set out in the Potsdam Proclamation. On Oct. 25 that year, the Chinese government announced that it was resuming its exercise of sovereignty over Taiwan. A ceremony to accept Japan's surrender in Taiwan Province of the China war theater of the Allied powers was held in Taipei. From that point forward, China had recovered Taiwan de jure and de facto through a host of documents with international legal effect. Taiwan's status as an inalienable part of the Chinese territory was thereby reaffirmed, and the question of Taiwan's status was resolved. However, an unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. The fact that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait have yet to be fully reunified is a scar left by history on the Chinese nation, but the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Driven by their political interests and secessionist agenda, Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and other secessionist forces have repeatedly claimed that Taiwan's status remains undetermined, distorted historical accounts in textbooks, pursued educational policies that remove Chinese cultural elements, and propagated a separatist narrative in an attempt to sever historical ties across the Strait and mislead younger generations in Taiwan. Since Lai Ching-te took office in 2024, the DPP authorities have conspicuously avoided mentioning China's victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and China's recovery of Taiwan. The DPP authorities have also repeatedly downplayed or whitewashed Japan's colonial rule over Taiwan. Such actions betray the fundamental interests of the Chinese nation. Achieving national reunification is a responsibility shared by all Chinese people, including people in Taiwan. The establishment of the Taiwan Recovery Day enables people on both sides of the Strait to commemorate this historic moment together. The Taiwan question originated in a weak and ravaged China, and will be resolved as China achieves national rejuvenation. Commemorating Taiwan's recovery today is an opportunity to draw strength and resolve from the sacrifices of the war and the recovery of lost territory, while reaffirming the determination and confidence to advance national reunification. item.title: Cross-Strait fishery ties strengthened
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
Cross-Strait fishery ties strengthened Source: China DailyUpdated: 2026-10-24
Taiwan fishery operators expressed strong confidence in the Chinese mainland market at a ceremony held on Friday in Xiamen, Fujian province, the mainland's coastal gateway to Taiwan, marking a major step toward streamlining the entry of seafood products from the island. Around 200 cross-Strait guests attended the event to witness the inauguration of a dedicated Taiwan fishery exhibition and sales center in Xiamen. It followed a recent trade initiative involving the introduction of about 350 metric tons of specialty Taiwan seafood, including grouper and threadfin. The ceremony marked a milestone in cross-Strait fishery cooperation, driven by 10 measures introduced by the mainland in April to promote trade, travel and cultural exchanges. The measures followed a high-profile meeting between leaders of the Communist Party of China and the Chinese Kuomintang. Figures from mainland authorities showed that sales of fishery products from Taiwan rose 35.5 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters of this year. Song Tao, head of both the Taiwan Work Office of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at the event that on the political basis of adhering to the 1992 Consensus — which embodies the one-China principle — both sides of the Taiwan Strait had continued to promote the implementation of the 10 measures and achieved positive progress. Song said that joint efforts could fully address the challenges faced by Taiwan fishermen, open up new pathways, secure their livelihoods and improve their overall well-being. He expressed hope that Taiwan compatriots would resolutely oppose "Taiwan independence" separatism and external interference, and work together with their mainland counterparts to safeguard peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait, while promoting the peaceful and integrated development of cross-Strait relations. Chang Jung-kung, vice-chairman of the KMT, said that exporting seafood to the mainland improved the well-being of grassroots fishers in Taiwan while offering mainland consumers more choices. This mutually beneficial cooperation has enabled compatriots on both sides to improve their standard of living, he said, adding that the KMT remained committed to collaborating with all sectors to promote the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations. Han Ying-huan, chairman of the Taiwan Businessmen Association in Xiamen, said: "We hope to take this chance to market Taiwan's fine aquatic products to the Chinese mainland for compatriots here to enjoy and advance cross-Strait exchanges." Hsieh Lung-yin, chairman of the Fishermen's Association in Taiwan, said that compatriots on both sides are one family, and that these measures fully reflected care for the well-being of Taiwan's grassroots fishers. "Xiamen is like a second home to me, as I first came here over 30 years ago to sell squid," Hsieh said. "We are deeply grateful that the mainland has streamlined import formalities and given us the green light, and the entire process is now running smoothly." A green channel for Taiwan fishery products was established in Xiamen in August. Through advance declarations and scheduled customs clearance, the processing time at the port for fresh Taiwan seafood was reduced to less than two hours. Chen Jinlai, deputy chief of the Gaoqi border inspection station in Xiamen, said that dedicated channels and online preclearance enable Taiwan vessels to start unloading as soon as they arrive. "This ensures that fish products move from the vessel to the dining table as quickly as possible, preserving their freshness and market value," he said. Related Stories

item.title: DPP slammed for betraying nation, history
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
DPP slammed for betraying nation, history Source: chinadaily.com.cnUpdated: 2026-10-22
The Chinese mainland has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities for barring people on the island from attending an event scheduled on the mainland in November to mark the 160th birth anniversary of Sun Yat-sen, saying the move betrays the nation and its history. Sun, a founding figure of the Chinese Kuomintang party and a revered revolutionary leader, died in 1925 in Beijing. His remains rest at the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing, the capital of Jiangsu province. The commemorative event aims to carry forward Sun's noble spirit of upholding national unity and striving for national rejuvenation, Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said on Wednesday. The event aims to unite all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots, in opposing "Taiwan independence" separatism and external interference and in promoting cross-Strait exchanges and integration, she added. Recently, Taiwan's "mainland affairs council" claimed that the commemoration would promote the idea of "anti-'independence' and pro-reunification". For the first time, it issued an explicit ban on participation in the event, saying that it would deny permission to anyone wanting to travel to the mainland to attend the commemoration, including county and city heads. Zhang, the mainland spokeswoman, accused the DPP authorities of resorting to every possible means to obstruct and restrict cross-Strait exchanges while intimidating and suppressing people in Taiwan. The decision "exposes the vicious intentions" of the DPP authorities "to obstruct cross-Strait exchanges and suppress Taiwan compatriots, betray the nation and history, split the country and stoke confrontation across the Taiwan Strait", Zhang said. "Their actions will inevitably meet with opposition and condemnation from all Chinese people," she added. Despite the DPP authorities' efforts to decouple the island's industries from the mainland market, latest statistics show robust growth in cross-Strait trade and people-to-people exchanges. In September, the value of Taiwan's exports to the mainland reached $20.6 billion, up 30.2 percent year-on-year, while its imports from the mainland totaled $13.5 billion, up 59.1 percent year-on-year, according to data released by Taiwan's finance department. According to the General Administration of Customs, the value of cross-Strait trade reached $301.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 30.3 percent year-on-year. The mainland's exports to Taiwan totaled $84.9 billion, up 37.3 percent, while its imports from Taiwan reached $216.3 billion, up 27.8 percent. Zhang said these figures demonstrate that cross-Strait industrial and supply chains remain stable and strong, and that markets on both sides of the Strait will never be decoupled, adding that economic exchanges and shared development across the Strait are an unstoppable trend. She emphasized that the DPP's moves to obstruct cross-Strait economic exchanges and cooperation and push for decoupling of supply chains to serve external forces are doomed to fail. Despite the DPP's standing travel curbs, 2.49 million trips by Taiwan residents to the mainland were recorded from January to August, up 19.6 percent year-on-year, according to data released by Taiwan authorities. Noting that attempts to prevent Taiwan residents from visiting the mainland are "absurd and futile", the spokeswoman urged the DPP authorities to abandon political maneuvering, withdraw unreasonable restrictions and facilitate cultural exchanges across the Strait. According to media reports, the DPP authorities have rejected an application by mainland actor Zhang Linghe, who has gained popularity in Taiwan for his drama Pursuit of Jade, to hold a fan meeting on the island. In response, the spokeswoman criticized the DPP for politicizing cross-Strait cultural exchanges, obstructing people-to-people interactions and disregarding public sentiment. Related Stories

item.title: China says no gray zone on Taiwan question
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
China says no gray zone on Taiwan question Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-10-22
BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- There is no gray area on the Taiwan question, and the Philippine side should abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Thursday. Mao made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on attempts by the Philippines to explore deeper cooperation with Taiwan region to address so-called "gray zone" activities despite Manila's one-China policy. "Any external exchanges conducted by China's Taiwan region must be handled in strict accordance with the one-China principle," Mao stressed. Related Stories

item.title: DPP's push for cross-Strait decoupling doomed to fail: mainland spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
DPP's push for cross-Strait decoupling doomed to fail: mainland spokesperson Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-10-22
BEIJING, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- A mainland spokesperson on Wednesday said attempts by Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities to decouple the island's industries from the mainland market are doomed to fail. Speaking at a regular press briefing, Zhang Han, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said the DPP authorities had been desperately obstructing economic exchanges across the Taiwan Strait and catering to external forces. According to official data, trade between the mainland and Taiwan totaled 301.2 billion U.S. dollars in the first nine months of this year, up 30.3 percent year on year. Mainland imports from Taiwan reached 216.3 billion U.S. dollars, an increase of 27.8 percent. "These figures fully demonstrate that cross-Strait industrial and supply chains have become more resilient and that markets on both sides of the Strait will never be decoupled," Zhang said, adding that economic exchanges and shared development across the Strait are an unstoppable trend. The spokesperson also responded to recent remarks by a Taiwan economic official regarding plans by the island's authorities to tighten controls on AI chip exports to the mainland and launch restriction measures that "correspond to U.S. ones." She criticized the DPP authorities for disregarding the interests of Taiwan's industries and businesses, while following the United States in lockstep to pursue their own political interests, obstructing and restricting normal business operations. "The mainland is committed to greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology," Zhang said. "External blockades have never been able to hold back our progress, and they will be even less able to do so in the future." The Chinese mainland's AI core industry was estimated to have exceeded 1.2 trillion yuan in 2025. By the end of September, its smart computing power reached 2,592 EFLOPS, up 146 percent year on year -- EFLOPS refers to a unit measuring computing performance, with each unit representing 1 quintillion floating-point operations per second. Zhang warned that the DPP authorities' restriction measures would only benefit opportunists pursuing "Taiwan independence" at the expense of Taiwan's industries and ordinary people, as they are squandering the competitive strengths of the island's industries built through generations of hard work by professionals, entrepreneurs and researchers. item.title: Mainland to strengthen CPC-KMT platform for protecting Taiwan people's rights
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
Mainland to strengthen CPC-KMT platform for protecting Taiwan people's rights Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-10-22
BEIJING, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese mainland will work to improve the operation and effectiveness of a cross-Strait platform established by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT), a spokesperson said Wednesday. The platform has maintained effective operations over the years through regular meetings, case referrals and other forms of cooperation, making itself an important channel for people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait to lodge complaints, seek advice and assistance, and protect their legitimate rights and interests, Zhang Han, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular news briefing. Since the beginning of this year, the Taiwan Work Office of the CPC Central Committee and the KMT have held multiple consultations to improve the platform's operations and effectiveness, and they have reached a consensus on further cooperation, she said. The two sides will maintain regular communication and provide timely feedback, and the platform will offer Taiwan residents professional legal services, Zhang said. They will also work to enhance assistance for Taiwan residents facing temporary difficulties, help people search for missing relatives and provide humanitarian care, she added. The two sides of the Strait established an investment dispute settlement mechanism in 2012 under a cross-Strait investment protection agreement reached on a common political foundation of the 1992 Consensus. However, the mechanism was suspended in May 2016 because Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities refused to recognize the 1992 Consensus, which embodies the one-China principle, Zhang said. The mainland is willing to engage in dialogue on resuming the mechanism's operations, provided that the DPP authorities recognize the 1992 Consensus, Zhang said. The Taiwan question stems from a civil war fought between the forces led by the CPC and the KMT about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, while the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Related Stories

Mainland denounces Taiwan authorities for hindering cross-Strait exchanges Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-10-21
BEIJING, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized the Taiwan authorities for barring relevant people on the island from attending the commemorative event held on the mainland marking the 160th anniversary of the birth of Sun Yat-sen. Sun, a founding figure of the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) and a revered revolutionary leader who played a pivotal role in overthrowing imperial rule in China, died in 1925 in Beijing. Zhang Han, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, noted that the grand commemoration of Sun's legacy is intended to inherit and carry forward his noble spirit of upholding national unity and striving for national rejuvenation. She stressed that the move by Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities to obstruct cross-Strait exchanges and suppress Taiwan compatriots fully exposes their vicious intentions of betraying the nation and history, seeking to split the country, and stoking confrontation across the Taiwan Strait. The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the KMT about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. item.title: Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-02-11
BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday denounced Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for ignoring the heinous crimes committed by Japan during its colonial rule over Taiwan, describing their flattering remarks toward Japan as utterly disgraceful. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media inquiry about Lai's intention to work with Japan to "deal with regional challenges." Zhu also urged the Japanese side to retract Sanae Takaichi's erroneous remarks on Taiwan, handle Taiwan-related issues prudently, and abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions. item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for imposing restrictions and obstacles on cross-Strait exchanges in pursuit of their "Taiwan independence" agenda and selfish gains. The DPP authorities, led by Lai Ching-te, are the biggest obstacle to cross-Strait interactions and their acts have drawn strong criticism from various sectors in Taiwan, Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press briefing on Wednesday. Zhu expressed the hope that Taiwan compatriots will firmly oppose the retrogressive actions of the DPP authorities and promote exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait in various fields. She noted that cross-Strait flight routes have been disrupted due to interference from the DPP authorities, with previously operated destinations yet to resume normal operations. In 2025, the average passenger load factor on cross-Strait routes reached 80 percent, reflecting the strong need for direct flights between the two sides of the Strait, Zhu said. "We hope that the Taiwan side will heed public opinion and lift unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transport as soon as possible," she added.
